items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: Billy Harper with Max Roach. You know they came up through this stuff... I want the adventurous spirit of these guys. You know? To keep looking. That’s what the Cookers I think grabs.

ctx.x: I see. Have they ever talked about back in the earlier parts of their career I think critics and authors sometimes like to make an issue of race in jazz. And I’m wondering if you hear that from these musicians?

I hear stuff about how they’re treated. You know I don’t think it’s in jazz, I think it’s in the world they live in. Like Billy Harper went to North Texas State and so did I. So one of our first conversations was like wow, North Texas State, it was a little different for a little Jewish boy from Queens. And then he told me his story and I’m like [holds up hands]. You know? “I couldn’t live on campus. I had to live in a little shack on the other side of the tracks and I had to walk two miles to school and finally…

but have found a way to (a) sort of find the beauty in it, (b) you know, be very practical about things. I’ll tend to get more caught up in little things because well I’ll say I’m privileged maybe. I don’t know. But it’s never a thing, you know, they’re very nice to me. You know I think you know in the end people are people. There are differences but I mean I think at this point I don’t have to prove it to them but I think they know my heart’s in the right place. You know? I put — and more importantly it’s a…
